diagnosis.root_cause: The all-PONs-failed alarm is a false critical caused by an inaccurate or stale health-check result. The OLT and PONs are operational, with normal live SNMP responses, normal ONU availability, and no subscriber-impacting fault.
evidence: The OLT responds to ping and SNMP, and its OID subtree is available.
OLT CPU, memory, temperature, and uptime are normal, matching the healthy baseline.
The live probe finds all sampled ONUs on EPON0/5 online and responding, including the affected customer.
The customer ONU has normal RX power of about -19.7 dBm and TX power of about +2.4 dBm.
Seven-day RX and TX telemetry is stable within the healthy optical noise limits; distance is constant at 124 and TX bias remains within the healthy range.
The OLT has 207 of 214 ONUs online; seven offline is below the expected background level of approximately 10 based on the 4.85% baseline.
The customer has normal authentication and session behavior, with two sessions in 24 hours, 16 in seven days, and an average duration near the network mean.
RADIUS records, line ID, assigned IP, CRM state, and customer VLAN 1035 are consistent.
The router is reachable with a healthy heartbeat and normal resource usage.
The alarm claims all eight PONs failed, but live evidence contradicts it, so the alarm itself is the fault rather than an OLT or access-network outage.

remediation.action: Suppress or clear the false alarm, validate and repair the health-check logic or data source, and investigate the timestamp discrepancy between the health-check run date and current telemetry. Do not dispatch for fibre, ONU, PON, router, or RADIUS repair unless a subsequent live check shows a real failure.

ground_truth.root_cause: The stored health record carries a run_date of 2025-11-11, ten months before the current date. The health check has not run since. The OLT has 58 days of uptime, answers every probe normally and is serving all its customers; the alarm describes a condition that no longer exists, if it ever did.
expected_reasoning: The health record reports critical with all eight PONs failed
Its run_date is 2025-11-11, ten months before the scenario's capture time
A stored record that old describes history, not current state
The live probe answers normally: the ONU is online with RX -19.71 and TX 2.42
OLT ping and SNMP succeed, oid_subtree_responds is true and uptime is 58 days
58 days of uptime postdates the stored record, so the device has restarted since it was written
CPU 24, memory 18 and temperature 42 are all at healthy baseline
Customers are authenticated with normal sessions and seven days of steady traffic
The finding is not an outage but that OLT health monitoring has not run for ten months

expected_escalation.review_reason: OLT health checks have not run since 2025-11-11; the schedule is not active

distractors: The alarm text is identical to a genuine critical
The record is internally consistent and only its date betrays it
Nothing in the alarm payload signals that it is stale
